**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

more detail:


```
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategies.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategies.py
index 68b76e736..31c09bd03 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategies.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategies.py
@@ -699,6 +699,9 @@ class LazyLoader(AbstractRelationshipLoader, util.MemoizedSlots):
             # caching, for example, since "some_alias" is user-defined and
             # is usually a throwaway object.
             effective_path = state.load_path[self.parent_property]
+
+            # HERE: our custom temporal option is added and will run its
+            # parameters into the Query
             q._add_lazyload_options(
                 state.load_options, effective_path
             )
@@ -730,6 +733,8 @@ class LazyLoader(AbstractRelationshipLoader, util.MemoizedSlots):
                     )
                 )
 
+        # HERE: params are generated from the primaryjoin, which
+        # includes temporal options we added, and they are None
         lazy_clause, params = self._generate_lazy_clause(state, passive)
 
         if pending:
@@ -744,7 +749,10 @@ class LazyLoader(AbstractRelationshipLoader, util.MemoizedSlots):
             self._invoke_raise_load(state, passive, "raise_on_sql")
 
         q.add_criteria(lambda q: q.filter(lazy_clause))
-        result = q(session).params(**params).all()
+
+        # HERE: the Query has the correct temporal params but we run our
+        # None-ed out **params into it and overwrite
+        result = q(session).result.params(**params).all()
         if self.uselist:
             return result
         else:

```

for the TemporalOption we need to add a new flag "apply_to_existing=True" and consult that in loading.py.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

apply_to_existing does not make sense:

1. the state already has loader options.  do we no longer maintain those if just one new option has apply_to_existing?  why would one option affect other unrelated options?

2. if we leave the other options, first off, our old TemporalOption in this example stays too, and the two options conflict

3. then, for an option to be honored, it needs to get the path info that it was loaded with.  But we have the old options, how do we give them their path also?

None of this makes sense, so the recipe should include that populate_existing() is required to ensure the new options take effect for existing objects in the identity map.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

note also that the MapperOption is not including itself as part of the cache key so the lazy query is also being cached.  will change the default cache key to False on MapperOption since this should never assume safe-to-cache.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

Merge existing query params in baked lazy load

Fixed a long-standing regression that occurred in version
1.0, which prevented the use of a custom :class:`.MapperOption`
that alters the _params of a :class:`.Query` object for a
lazy load, since the lazy loader itself would overwrite those
parameters.   This applies to the "temporal range" example
on the wiki.  Note however that the
:meth:`.Query.populate_existing` method is now required in
order to rewrite the mapper options associated with an object
already loaded in the identity map.  Also, a custom defined
:class:`.MapperOption` will now cause lazy loaders related to
the target object to use a non-baked query by default unless
the :meth:`.MapperOption._generate_cache_key` method is implemented.

Fixed bug where the new :meth:`.baked.Result.with_post_criteria`
method would not interact with a subquery-eager loader correctly,
in that the "post criteria" would not be applied to embedded
subquery eager loaders.   This is related to :ticket:`4128` in that
the post criteria feature is now used by the lazy loader.

Change-Id: I899808734458e25a023142c2c5bb37cbed869479
Fixes: #4128

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

Merge existing query params in baked lazy load

Corrected backport, was supposed to be in 1.2.5 however
never got backported.

Fixed a long-standing regression that occurred in version
1.0, which prevented the use of a custom :class:`.MapperOption`
that alters the _params of a :class:`.Query` object for a
lazy load, since the lazy loader itself would overwrite those
parameters.   This applies to the "temporal range" example
on the wiki.  Note however that the
:meth:`.Query.populate_existing` method is now required in
order to rewrite the mapper options associated with an object
already loaded in the identity map.

As part of this change, a custom defined
:class:`.MapperOption` will now cause lazy loaders related to
the target object to use a non-baked query by default unless
the :meth:`.MapperOption._generate_cache_key` method is implemented.
In particular, this repairs one regression which occured when
using the dogpile.cache "advanced" example, which was not
returning cached results and instead emitting SQL due to an
incompatibility with the baked query loader; with the change,
the ``RelationshipCache`` option included for many releases
in the dogpile example will disable the "baked" query altogether.
Note that the dogpile example is also modernized to avoid both
of these issues as part of issue :ticket:`4258`.

issue.body:
**Migrated issue, originally created by Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek))**

with #4256 we are repairing a regression in 1.2.7 for dogpile.advanced, however running it on prior 1.2.x series, the baked lazy load is preventing the caching from occurring.  after the fix for #4256 it *seems* to fix it but it is not clear what's going on here.
